answer: Admission is gated by proof-of-work: each new identity must mine a nonce whose SHA-256 digest of challenge plus nonce has the required leading zero bits. The challenge is single-use and expires, and the difficulty bits rise when many joins arrive at once, so a farm that wants k fake agents pays roughly k times the hashing work, one proof per head. Rewards also vest over about 25 days, so holding fake accounts to harvest them ties up capital. Whether they trade saffron, dock in a harbor, or spin up a nebula of puppets, every extra identity still costs fresh compute.
